title: Just entered the US
ask: Does your new I-94 show the right class of admission (H-1B, H-4 or F-1) and the right "Admit Until" date (D/S for F-1)?
why: The I-94, not the visa stamp or the I-797, controls how long you may stay. Officers sometimes shorten it to your passport's expiry date or enter the wrong class.

title: Fix an I-94 problem
short: Fix the problem with your I-94
ask: Have you asked a CBP Deferred Inspection office to correct the I-94, or, if it was cut to your passport expiry, planned an I-539 extension or a re-entry with a renewed passport before it runs out?
why: Staying past the I-94 date, even with a valid I-797 or I-20, means you are out of status. Deferred Inspection fixes CBP mistakes; a passport-based short date needs a new I-94 in time.

title: Moved home
short: Did you report your new address?
ask: Did you report your new address within 10 days: AR-11 with USCIS (and on every pending case), and for F-1 to your DSO or in the SEVP Portal?
why: Address reporting is a legal requirement, and missed USCIS mail (requests for evidence, cards, interview notices) is one of the most common ways cases go wrong.

title: Passport expires within a year
short: Have you started renewing your passport?
ask: Have you started renewing your Indian passport?
why: At your next entry CBP may cut your I-94 to the passport expiry date, and USCIS filings generally need a passport valid for the whole period requested.

title: Travelling outside the US
short: Is your visa stamp valid for return?
ask: Is the visa stamp in your passport valid on the day you fly back, and in the right class?
why: You can stay in the US on an expired stamp, but you cannot re-enter on one. An approved I-797 is not a visa.

title: No valid visa stamp
short: Have you booked a visa appointment?
ask: Have you booked a consulate appointment that fits your trip, in the country where you are a national or resident?
why: Since September 2025 the State Department expects nonimmigrant visa applicants to apply in their country of nationality or residence, so routine third-country stamping in Canada or Mexico is no longer a safe plan. Waits in India vary by post and can run months.

title: Travelling outside the US
short: Do you still qualify for a dropbox renewal?
ask: If you were counting on a dropbox (interview waiver) renewal, have you confirmed you still qualify?
why: The State Department narrowed interview waivers in September 2025. Most H-1B, H-4 and F-1 applicants should now expect an in-person interview, which changes how far ahead you must book.

title: Travelling outside the US
ask: Before a visa interview, are your social-media profiles set to public and listed on the DS-160?
why: The State Department extended its online-presence review to F-1 applicants in 2025 and to H-1B and H-4 applicants from December 2025; private accounts can delay a decision.

title: Travelling outside the US
short: Is your passport valid for the trip?
ask: Is your passport valid well beyond your return date, and will you carry your latest I-797 (or I-20 with a recent travel signature), recent pay stubs and an employment letter?
why: CBP admits you only until your passport expires, and officers can ask for proof you are still working or studying in status.

title: Good housekeeping
short: Have you set up your USCIS account?
ask: Do you have a USCIS online account and a folder with every I-797, I-94 and EAD you have ever received?
why: Every future filing asks for your full status history, and online accounts show notices days before paper mail arrives.

title: Good housekeeping
short: Would you spot a visa scam call?
ask: Do you know that USCIS, ICE and consulates never phone to demand payment, gift cards or passport details?
why: Indian nationals are a frequent target of impersonation calls threatening deportation. Hang up and check your case in your USCIS account instead.
